text:
alex.h: Heads-up — noticed a weird auth+embed parity issue in the new Next starter (https://github.com/redwood-inference/next-starter-lite). SSR requests to /api/embed sometimes get 401s during bursty traffic. Repro steps: clone, npm run dev, open two tabs and trigger embed gen quickly.

maria: ugh that sounds like our token refresh race again? :eyes: can you paste the serverless handler?

alex.h: sure — handler is tiny, basically:
```js
export default async function handler(req, res) {
  const token = process.env.RW_API_KEY; // used for server-side calls
  const r = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
    body: JSON.stringify({input: req.body.text})
  });
  if (!r.ok) return res.status(r.status).send(await r.text());
  res.json(await r.json());
}
```

alex.h: interesting part is the JS SDKs we used for the starter (llamaindex client shim) handle retries differently than the python examples. The starter currently embeds via raw fetch to show minimal deps, but that means we don't get the SDK's automatic refresh/retry hooks.

samir: confirmed — seen similar in staging when a KMS rotation overlapped with an influx of SSR requests. JS fetch + ephemeral token in env can produce transient 401s that the SDK would have retried. Quick workaround: add a tiny client-side debounce so SSR embed requests are serialized, or swap to the official JS SDK call which includes transparent retry.

maria: could also be a timing issue where Vercel cold starts mean process.env not yet populated? but env is baked at build — less likely. Do you have logs?

alex.h: attaching a snippet from vite dev logs:
```
[17:03:12] POST /api/embed 401 Unauthorized {"error":"invalid_token"}
[17:03:12] POST /api/embed 200 OK (retry)
[17:03:13] POST /api/embed 401 Unauthorized {"error":"invalid_token"}
```

alex.h: so sometimes a retry works (manual refresh), sometimes not. Also noticed telemetry in Console shows embed events attributed to the wrong route — looks like our sample's telemetry wrapper is using a global route name instead of the request path.

tasha: file a short GH issue with stacktrace and steps? I can take the sample patch to add SDK usage + a feature flag defaulting to raw-fetch so we keep the minimal-example behaviour. Then we can add a note in the README about SSR auth caveats.

alex.h: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/next-starter-lite/issues/142 — includes logs and proposed fix (switch to @redwood/sdk-js embedClient.embed(...)). Leaving the raw-fetch snippet behind a `USE_RAW_FETCH=true` env flag.

samir: nice. For immediate devex mitigation we should also add a line in the Quickstart (docs/getting-started.md) calling out: "If you run into 401s under concurrent SSR, try setting USE_RAW_FETCH=false to use SDK retry logic."

maria: FYI the root cause here might be SDK parity — the JS SDK auto-retries on 401 with a single refresh attempt; the Python client currently does two refresh attempts and treats 429/5xx differently. We should sync on consistent retry semantics across SDKs (backoff, max attempts, which status codes trigger refresh).

tasha: agree — I'll create a short RFC in product-engineering for SDK parity on retry semantics. In the meantime I'll land the sample patch + README note.

ci-bot: deploy queued for branch alex/embed-sample-fix — CI running tests.

alex.h: thanks all — will monitor telemetry after merge. if anyone sees an odd attribution in Console, ping me.

maria: great thread. small follow-up: can we add a tiny test in the sample that simulates concurrent embed requests so this doesn't regress? 1-liner using Promise.all.

alex.h: good call — adding that test in the PR now.

tasha: merging PR after CI green. :shipit:

ci-bot: build passed. deploy complete.

alex.h: deployed and verified — no 401s in 20-min smoke with the SDK path. I'll close the GH issue after a day of production traffic.
